title: What does MPTokenAuthorize do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of MPTokenAuthorize and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, MPTokenAuthorize establishes MPT holding permission or changes a holder's authorization for an issuance. [1]

A holder can establish the ledger entry needed to receive an MPT, while an issuer can authorize or unauthorize a holder where the issuance requires it. These roles have different semantics. The issuance identifier determines the asset; a familiar token name does not. Authorization does not itself mint a balance or attest to a customer's real-world identity. [1]

The MPTokenAuthorize reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using MPTokenAuthorize, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
